## What is LADAL? {#about}

The **Language Technology and Data Analysis Laboratory (LADAL)** is a collaborative, open-access research infrastructure dedicated to supporting researchers, students, and educators who work with language data. Established in 2019 by the [School of Languages and Cultures](https://languages-cultures.uq.edu.au/) at the [University of Queensland](https://www.uq.edu.au/), LADAL provides free, high-quality tutorials, tools, and training in language technology, data analysis, and computational methods — with no programming experience required to get started.

LADAL is part of the [**Language Data Commons of Australia (LDaCA)**](https://ldaca.edu.au/), a national research infrastructure providing researchers with searchable language datasets, a browser-based notebook environment, comprehensive learning resources, and expert guidance. LDaCA is a co-investment partnership with the [Australian Research Data Commons (ARDC)](https://ardc.edu.au/) through the HASS and Indigenous Research Data Commons, enabled by the Australian Government's National Collaborative Research Infrastructure Strategy (NCRIS).

## Our Principles {#principles}

LADAL is committed to FAIR and open science principles in everything we produce.

```{=html}
<div class="principles-grid">
  <div class="principle-card">
    <div class="principle-icon">🔍</div>
    <h4>Findable</h4>

  </div>
  <div class="principle-card aqua">
```

## Who LADAL is For {#audience}

LADAL is designed for anyone who works with language data, regardless of background or experience level. **No prerequisites required** — you don't need prior programming experience, a mathematical background, or expensive software licences.

```{=html}
<div class="audience-grid">
  <div class="audience-card">
    <h4>🔤 Linguists</h4>
    <p>Corpus linguistics, computational linguistics, sociolinguistics, and more.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="audience-card">
    <h4>📚 Digital Humanists</h4>
    <p>Text analytics, discourse analysis, and computational approaches to humanities research.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="audience-card">
    <h4>🔭 Social Scientists</h4>
    <p>Quantitative and qualitative methods for language-based social research.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="audience-card">
    <h4>🏭 Industry Practitioners</h4>
    <p>NLP applications, text analytics, and applied language technology.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="audience-card">
    <h4>🌱 Complete Beginners</h4>
    <p>Zero programming experience? Our beginner tutorials start from scratch.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="audience-card">
    <h4>🎓 Students &amp; Researchers</h4>
    <p>Undergraduate, postgraduate, and academic researchers at any career stage.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Why R? {#why-r}

LADAL primarily uses R because it is ideally suited to language research: free and open-source, purpose-built for statistical analysis, powerful for text processing, and capable of producing publication-quality visualisations. R also supports fully reproducible research workflows through R Markdown and Quarto — this very website is built with R.

With over 20,000 packages available and a large, supportive community, R is both comprehensive and accessible. While R is our foundation, we are expanding to include Python tutorials to serve the broader research community.

[Learn more: Why R? →](/tutorials/whyr/whyr.html)

## What We Offer {#offer}

LADAL provides three core resource types, all free and open access:

```{=html}
<div class="audience-grid">
  <div class="audience-card">
    <h4>📖 Tutorials</h4>
    <p>Step-by-step guides covering data science basics, text analytics, statistics, visualisation, and more — with fully runnable R code.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="audience-card">
    <h4>🎓 Courses</h4>
    <p>Short and long-form courses for structured learning, suitable for self-study or classroom use.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="audience-card">
    <h4>🛠️ Tools</h4>
    <p>Browser-based notebook tools that let you run analyses without installing anything — upload your own data and go.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Frequently Asked Questions {#faq}

```{=html}
<div class="faq-grid">
  <div class="faq-item">
    <h4>Do I need to know programming?</h4>
    <p>No. Our beginner tutorials assume zero programming experience.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="faq-item">
    <h4>Is LADAL really free?</h4>
    <p>Yes, completely. No hidden costs, no paywalls, no registration required.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="faq-item">
    <h4>Can I use LADAL for teaching?</h4>
    <p>Absolutely. All content is freely available for educational use.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="faq-item">
    <h4>Do I need to install R?</h4>
    <p>No — we offer browser-based notebooks. We do recommend installing R for serious or sustained work.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="faq-item">
    <h4>How do I get help if I'm stuck?</h4>
    <p>Email us at <a href="mailto:ladal@uq.edu.au">ladal@uq.edu.au</a>, check the tutorial FAQs, or search online R communities.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="faq-item">
    <h4>Can I contribute?</h4>
    <p>Yes! We welcome contributions. <a href="mailto:ladal@uq.edu.au">Contact us</a> to discuss opportunities.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="faq-item">
    <h4>Is there support for languages other than English?</h4>
    <p>Most content is currently in English, but we are actively working on multilingual resources.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="faq-item">
    <h4>How often is content updated?</h4>
    <p>Regularly. We continuously improve tutorials based on feedback and new developments in the field.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="faq-item">
    <h4>Can I download the tutorials?</h4>
    <p>Yes — all code and materials are downloadable from each tutorial page.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="faq-item">
    <h4>Who funds LADAL?</h4>
    <p>LADAL is supported by the University of Queensland and is part of LDaCA, funded through ARDC/NCRIS.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Acknowledgments {#acknowledgments}

LADAL exists because of the generous support of many individuals and institutions.

**Institutional support:** University of Queensland School of Languages and Cultures · Language Data Commons of Australia (LDaCA) · Australian Research Data Commons (ARDC) · HASS and Indigenous Research Data Commons

**Funding:** NCRIS · Australian Research Data Commons · Australian Government · University of Queensland

**Foundational contributions:** Early LADAL tutorials drew substantially on the work of [Andreas Niekler](https://www.uni-leipzig.de/en/profile/mitarbeiter/dr-andreas-niekler) (University of Leipzig) and [Gregor Wiedemann](https://leibniz-hbi.de/en/staff/gregor-wiedemann) (Leibniz Institute / HBI) — in particular their tutorial on R for Humanities Research. We gratefully acknowledge their foundational role in shaping LADAL's early content.

**Community:** Tutorial contributors and reviewers · Workshop participants · Our global user community · The open-source R community
